document.title: Ambassador Reviews Again GOP Policy on Afghanistan (Islamabad 00138)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan's Bin Laden Policy
document.note: [Secret] Heavily excised account of Ambassador William Milam's meeting with Foreign Minister Sartaj Aziz. The U.S. urged the GOP to get active in convincing the Taliban to expel Usama bin Ladin and to change its pro-Taliban policies. Aziz listened carefully but his response contained little that was new.

mentions.quote: THE AMBASSADOR MET JANUARY 7 WITH FOREIGN MINISTER SARTAT AZIZ.
THE AMBASSADOR MET JANUARY 7 WITH FOREIGN MINISTER SARTAT AZIZ.
AZIZ LISTENED VERY CAREFULLY TO OUR POINTS.

events.description: Ambassador Milam met Foreign Minister Sartaj Aziz, urging Pakistan to reconsider support for the Taliban and press them to expel bin Ladin.
Planned visit of A/S Inderfurth to Islamabad at the end of January 1999.
Ambassador Milam met FM Sartaj Aziz, urging Pakistan to reconsider Taliban support and press the Taliban to expel bin Ladin; Aziz's response contained little new.
A/S Karl Inderfurth planned to visit Islamabad at the end of January 1999; Aziz suggested a preparatory meeting beforehand.

key_claims: The U.S. Ambassador urged Pakistan to reconsider its four years of all-out support for the Taliban.
The U.S. asked Pakistan to use its influence to have the Taliban expel Usama bin Ladin to face justice.
Foreign Minister Sartaj Aziz listened carefully but offered little new in response.
Pakistan said it was willing to listen to U.S. advice and proposed a preparatory meeting before Inderfurth's visit.
